e2 project requirements — what a generated project must supply

The TF-M build reads its memory layout, its FSP driver sources and several load-bearing settings out of generated e2 studio projects. This is the contract those projects satisfy. Read it when you regenerate a project, change a solution, or add a part — PORTING.md is the wider procedure for a new part, and DESIGN.md §1 says why the projects are generated rather than edited.

Most of the contract is enforced at build time. Where a requirement is checked, the build stops with an #error naming the setting and the project, so a regeneration that drops something fails at compile time rather than on the board.

1. The three projects

The build takes three directories per part and toolchain, one per image:

VariableRoleRA6M5RA8M2
FSP_BL2_APP_DIRFSP driver modules for BL2, which is a flat buildra6m5_<tc>_mcubootra8m2_<tc>_mcuboot
FSP_S_APP_DIRdriver modules for the secure image, and the source of the layoutra6m5_<tc>_securera8m2_<tc>_CPU0_secure
FSP_NS_APP_DIRthe whole FSP application, built as tfm_nsra6m5_<tc>_nonsecurera8m2_<tc>_CPU0_nonsecure

<tc> is gcc or iar. Keep the pairing. A project set is generated for one toolchain and the TF-M build must use the matching one. Crossing them mostly works, because ra_gen/ and ra_cfg/ are toolchain-neutral and TF-M supplies its own linker script, but it is not the intended arrangement.

All three projects belong to one solution, which owns the partitioning for the set. Both toolchains describe the same part and feed one set of TrustZone boundary values, so their solutions have to agree on the layout.

2. Files only an e2 build produces

Regenerating is not enough. These are build outputs, so a project that has never been built in e2 cannot configure TF-M:

FileRead by
Debug/bsp_linker_info.hevery image. Filtered to its BSP_PARTITION_* defines at configure time, because the rest of the file declares C types a linker script cannot take
Debug/memory_regions.ld, Debug/memory_regions.icfthe non-secure link, and on RA8M2 the option-memory addresses, filtered into a generated option_settings.h
script/fsp.ldthe non-secure link, used as the scatter file

The build looks in Debug/. The standalone Smart Configurator writes these to the project root instead, which is one of the open items in moving the set to RASC.

3. The partition contract

bsp_linker_info.h must define these as _START and _SIZE pairs. The secure project's copy is the one parsed, because it is a strict superset: it carries the bootloader regions that the bootloader project's own copy omits.

GroupSymbols
BootloaderFLASH_BL_CPU0_S, RAM_BL_CPU0_S
Code and RAMFLASH_CPU0_S, FLASH_CPU0_C, FLASH_CPU0_N, RAM_CPU0_S, RAM_CPU0_C, RAM_CPU0_N
Slot markers__BL_0_P_H, __BL_0_P_T, __BL_0_S_H, __BL_0_S_T, and the same four for __BL_1
Storage, RA6M5DATA_FLASH_CPU0_S, DATA_FLASH_CPU0_N
Storage, RA8M2DATA_FLASH_CPU0_S, which must stay 0, and DF_EMULATION

Three geometry rules the layout has to keep, each asserted in <part>_layout_checks.c:

  • Partitions are contiguous and both slot pairs are the same size. fa_size is a sum of sizes while the trailer magic is placed from the address span, so a hole makes imgtool and bootutil disagree about where the magic goes. Such an image boots, then fails its first upgrade.
  • The non-secure-callable region ends exactly on the secure boundary, and its start sits inside the signed payload so the veneers are covered by the signature.
  • The header is 0x200 and both trailer partitions are zero-size end markers. MCUboot takes its trailer from the slot tail. TF-M's own defaults are 0x400, and those cache values are what imgtool signs with, so a mismatch places the payload 0x400 into a slot linked for 0x200. region_defs.h stops the build on it.

Secure data flash must be large enough for the NV counters, Protected Storage and Internal Trusted Storage together. flash_layout.h divides what it is given and stops below the minimum.

4. Modules, per project

A module reaches a TF-M image only if the port declares it. Enabling more in e2 is harmless for the standalone build, but produces a configure-time warning naming the module as not in any image.

ProjectModules the build needs
securebsp, flash, sce, agt
bootloaderbsp, flash
non-securewhatever the application needs; the whole tree is globbed
  • The flash driver is a different FSP module per part. RA6M5 takes r_flash_hp. RA8M2 takes r_mram, which appears in e2 as Flash with the MRAM implementation rather than Flash (r_flash_hp), and its instance is g_mram0 where RA6M5 has g_flash0.
  • The crypto engine directory under r_sce is discovered, not named: sce9 on RA6M5, rsip_e50d on RA8M2.
  • The SCE module in the secure project supplies the TRNG that PSA uses as its external RNG. Without it the secure image has no entropy source. Only the TRNG is taken; the rest is trimmed by --gc-sections.
  • AGT in the secure project, with a real interrupt priority. Disabled emits no vector entry at all, and the FLIH and SLIH suites then cannot raise an interrupt. Configuring it in the secure project is also what makes the interrupt secure.
  • Three modules are deliberately never built from the projects — the FSP crypto stack, rm_psa_crypto and rm_mcuboot_port — because the crypto and flash-map configuration they carry collides with TF-M's. FSP_MODULES_NEVER_BUILT enforces that. Their headers must still resolve, because the generated common_data.h and hal_data.h include them unconditionally even when nothing is instantiated.
  • Generated file names stay standard. The build excludes ra_gen/main.c, Source/startup.c and bsp_linker.c by name for the secure and bootloader images, because TF-M supplies all three. Renaming them makes the FSP versions collide at link.

5. Settings that are load-bearing

SettingWhereConsequence if wrong
Early BSP Initialization enabledsecure and bootloaderSystemCoreClock is zero after SystemInit() and the flash driver fails to open with FSP_ERR_FCLK
Main stack sizeall threeit replaces the g_init_info and g_main_stack that the excluded bsp_linker.c would have defined, and it must match the secure image stack size the build expects
Option-setting wordsbootloader onlythe bootloader project is the only one whose option settings reach an image. Editing them in the secure project has no effect and gives no warning

RA8M2 carries one guard per option word the port does not place, so a word enabled in e2 cannot be silently dropped. RA6M5 has none, because it places the three words it emits.

6. Launch configurations

setTZBoundaries must be false for every debug probe a launch names. It defaults to enabled, derives the boundaries from the launched project's symbols, and cannot handle a bootloader and a secure image that share the secure region: launched against the bootloader it marks everything secure and silently undoes a correct partition. DESIGN.md §7.2.

Leave erase code flash and erase data flash enabled on connect, so a stale storage area does not survive a reflash.

7. What a project cannot supply

  • The TrustZone boundaries. Nothing in the firmware programs them. They are set once per board with the Renesas Device Partition Manager and must be recomputed on any repartition against the granularity rule for the part. The values are in the part guides, RA6M5_SOLUTION.md and RA8M2_SOLUTION.md.
  • The option-memory placement rule. Each option word needs its own linker MEMORY region. One coalesced load segment zero-fills the memory between the words and writes values nobody chose. That is the failure that made two EK-RA6M4 boards un-erasable, it is invisible in the srec, and it lives in the TF-M linker scripts rather than in any project — but re-verify it after a layout change. GETTING_STARTED.md §6 has the check.
